context.problem_statement: Apply the Savitzky-Golay filter to denoise a noisy sensor time series. The signal contains a true sinusoidal component with additive Gaussian noise. Steps: (1) apply scipy.signal.savgol_filter with window_length=11 and polyorder=3, (2) compute Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) before and after filtering as: SNR_dB = 10 * log10(signal_power / noise_power), where signal_power = mean(signal^2), noise_power = mean((signal - true_signal)^2), (3) compare SNR improvement, (4) also apply a simple moving average (window=11) for comparison and compute its SNR, (5) report which filter performs better and why.
context.expert_knowledge: Savitzky-Golay fits a polynomial to each window, preserving peak shapes better than moving average. Larger window_length: more smoothing but more peak broadening. Higher polyorder: better peak preservation but less noise reduction. SNR improvement = SNR_after - SNR_before in dB. For sinusoidal signals, SG filter outperforms MA filter at preserving amplitude. Use scipy.signal.savgol_filter(y, window_length, polyorder).
